summary: A table whose cells the user moves among with the arrow keys, to read, select or act on them. It wraps the browser's own table.

tree.description: Rows can hold child rows that the user opens and closes: the table gets the treegrid role.

root.note: A block around the table; it scrolls when the table is wider.

table.note: A native table the author writes and marks with data-part="table". It gets the grid role, or treegrid, and is one stop in the Tab order.

keys.Home, End: The first or the last cell of the row.
keys.Control+Home, Control+End: The first cell of the first row, or the last cell of the last row.
keys.ArrowRight, ArrowLeft on a row (tree): Open or close the row, or move to its first cell or its parent row.
keys.Enter, F2 on a cell with several control: Move focus to the cell's first control.
keys.Tab, Shift+Tab inside such a cell: Move to the cell's next or previous control, wrapping; the arrow keys, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown are the control's.
keys.Escape, F2 inside such a cell: Move focus back to the cell; the grid's keys work again.

guidance.text: The author names the table with a caption, aria-label or aria-labelledby.

A cell that holds one plain control, such as a link, a button or a checkbox, hands focus to that control. A cell with several controls, or with one that takes text or uses the arrow keys, takes focus itself: Enter or F2 moves into it, Escape or F2 back out, and it carries data-editing while focus is inside. With tree, a row's level is its data-level attribute, and a row with child rows carries aria-expanded as the author wrote it.

notYet: Editing a cell's own text in place: the grid moves focus into a cell's controls, but does not turn a cell into a field.
